title: Batching Sherlock: workload prober, heuristic profile synthesis, and guarded continuous apply
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a continuous workload probing and heuristic synthesis engine (codename: Batching Sherlock) that produces safe, incremental batching + caching config updates for runtime. The engine should generate profiles from short-term telemetry, score candidate parameter sets via lightweight heuristics, and apply changes via a guarded gradual rollout with automatic rollback triggers.
problem_statement: Current batch/caching tuning is manual and brittle: engineers rely on offline profiles and ad-hoc thresholds. We lack a reliable online synthesizer that (1) detects microburst patterns and sequence-length shifts, (2) proposes batch/cache parameters that trade latency for cost, and (3) applies them without causing customer-visible regressions.
proposed_solution: Build a service that continuously samples per-route telemetry (IAT, seq_len, kv_hit_ratio, prefix_reuse), computes compact signatures, synthesizes candidate configs using a ranked heuristic ensemble (entropy-weighted batching, KV-alignment score, microburst-resilience), and enacts changes using shadow evaluation + stepwise canary (1->5->20% traffic) with SLO & cost guards. Provide a fallback and immediate rollback if latency P95 increases > 12% or error-rate delta > 0.4%.
design_decisions: Use 5-minute rolling windows for primary profiling, keep 1-hour aggregated history for trend detection
Represent workload signatures as a small vector: {avg_iat_ms, iat_p95_ms, seq_mean, seq_p90, kv_reuse_pct, entropy_of_prompt_lengths}
Heuristic ensemble weights are adjustable per-customer; start with global defaults learned from historical clusters
Shadow evaluations run on a 0% traffic shadow cluster to validate throughput and cache behavior before canarying
All config changes are labeled with origin: 'sherlock-auto' to enable audit and manual revert
technical_notes: Microburst detection: compute inter-arrival time CDF and flag when mass shifts under 30ms windows with >10% of requests
KV-alignment score: fraction of requests with overlapping prefix tokens * expected cache window; penalize configs that reduce expected reuse below 60%
Entropy-weighted batching: prefer larger batch sizes when prompt-length entropy is low to avoid latency variance
Safety net: limit max_batch_size to min(runtime_hardware_limit, baseline_max_batch*1.3)
Telemetry sources: per-route fast path from gateway + runtime token counters; enrich with tracing IDs for tail-latency attribution
acceptance_criteria: Service computes and stores workload signatures for 95% of active routes every 5 minutes
Synthesized candidate configs include explicit numeric values for: max_batch_size, target_batch_latency_ms, kv_prefetch_window_ms, autoscale_burst_threshold
Shadow evaluation validates throughput and kv-hit impact within a 24-hour window for at least 10 diverse routes
Canary rollout implements percent steps [1,5,20] with automated halt/rollback on guards
Dashboard shows before/after cost per 1M tokens and latency delta for each applied change
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local profiler sim (1 week)
Phase 1 (internal shadow): deploy to staging shadow cluster, validate against replay traces (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (canary): small set of non-critical customer routes (1-3) with strict SLO guards (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual expand): expand to broader cohort with automated monitoring and weekly review (ongoing)
Immediate rollback policy: auto-revert if P95 latency increases > 12% or error-rate delta > 0.4% for 10-minute window
tests: Unit tests for signature computation and heuristic scoring
Replay-based integration tests using historical production traces
Chaos test: simulate transient RPC failures during rollout to verify rollback resilience
Load test: validate that shadow evaluations do not exhaust GPU capacity
